name: Workspace (resizable primary region with yielding panels)
purpose: A page built around one primary region (an image, canvas, document page, map or board) with secondary information around it. The person can resize the primary region and hide the panels; the layout keeps the primary region primary and the panels yield first.
whenToUse: The page has one square or fixed-ratio region that is the task (an image editor canvas, a document page preview, a map, a game board) and its useful size depends on the screen and the person.
Secondary information (details, pages, notes, statistics) helps but is not needed all the time, and can be disclosed on demand.
The same page is used on a laptop, a large monitor and a tablet and one fixed region size would be wrong on one of them.
whenNotToUse: Text content with a reading measure (articles, documents being edited, feeds). A fixed maximum line length is correct there; this pattern is for regions whose useful size is open.
A dashboard, table or list that fills the width and has no single primary region.
Navigation. Panels carry content, never links to other areas (P14). Use the application sidebar.
A full screen or zen mode. Hiding the panels and choosing the largest size covers it without another state.
A region whose size the product must control exactly (a print preview at true size, a pixel-exact canvas). Use a fixed region and say why (P22).
anatomy: Toolbar (44px): panel toggles at both ends, size controls in the middle. Buttons are sm-icon-btn with a neutral --s2 fill.
Primary region: at least a square of the computed size, centered; optional header and footer above and below, measured and held at their peak.
Resize handle: a 24px slider button hanging outside the bottom right corner.
Left and right panels: content panes one step above the surface (--s2), equal reserve on both sides.
Drawer: a panel that cannot dock opens over a scrim as a dialog, 360px wide at most.
Scrim: rgba(8,9,9,.55), closes the drawer on click.

variants.description: Left panel, primary region and right panel in one row. Panels shrink from preferred to minimum width, then become drawers.
variants.useWhen: The workspace is at least 640px wide and a minimum-size region fits beside the open panels.

variants.description: Primary region on top at full width, open panels below as titled sections. Nothing hides behind a drawer.
variants.useWhen: A narrow screen, or open panels that cannot dock beside even a minimum-size region.

variants.description: One panel only. The other flank still reserves the same width so the region stays centered.
variants.useWhen: Only one of the two panels has content.

behavior: Geometry comes from the pure function in js/workspace-geometry.js (reference: src/ui/workspaceGeometry.ts). The host measures the workspace with a ResizeObserver and sets --sm-ws-size, --sm-ws-left, --sm-ws-right.
The responsive default is deliberately medium (at most 640px) and scales with the available space. The person's choice, when there is one, is only clamped for display.

A size choice is a preference, not a measurement: store the pick (null means default), never the clamped value. Store panel visibility per workspace and share one size across compatible workspaces. Guard every storage access.
Panels yield in order: shrink, drawer, stack. They stay mounted so their state survives.
Chrome above and below the region is measured; the peak since the workspace opened is used so the region never jumps.
Escape closes a drawer and returns focus to the toggle that opened it. A drawer that no longer applies closes by itself.
Status: provisional. Built from the principles and one real application; compare visually with the owner's references before treating it as reviewed.
accessibility: Resize handle: role=slider on a real button, aria-label, aria-orientation=horizontal, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext in pixels. Arrow keys step by 40px, Home and End jump to the limits.
Toolbar is role=toolbar with a label. Toggles use aria-pressed and a label that says what a press does. Size buttons are disabled at the limits, not hidden.
An open drawer is role=dialog with aria-modal=true and the panel title as its label; focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Escape closes, focus returns to the toggle.
Panels are labelled regions (section with aria-label), not aside and not navigation.
Touch: every control has an effective hit area of at least 40x40 CSS px (P18, CHK-020); the handle gains an invisible 44px extension.
Focus ring is the shared 1.5px --focus neutral ring on every control and on the focused panel.
Motion: none required. Nothing animates the size.
statusNote: Candidate for PR-0002, not part of any approved bundle. It depends on candidate principles P23 to P26 (feedback/proposals/PR-0002/candidate/principles.md), which are not yet approved, so they are not listed in principles. Open owner questions are in the proposal summary.
